lines: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Ten police personnel, including two senior officers, are killed in a clash after insurgents ambushed police vehicles in Kohat District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. (AP)

Insurgency in Jammu and Kashmir Three Central Reserve Police Force personnel are injured after militants opened fire on a CRPF checkpoint near Mir Bazar in Kulgam district, Jammu and Kashmir, India. Security forces launch a search operation to locate the attackers. (The Hindu)
The American ocean liner SS United States is sunk off the coast of Destin and Fort Walton Beach, Florida to become the world's largest artificial reef. (Pensacola News Journal)

2026 Iran war fuel crisis, German economic crisis The German cabinet approves draft legislation establishing a strategic natural gas reserve of 24 terawatt-hours, equivalent to approximately 10% of national storage capacity, to maintain gas supplies during emergencies. (AFP via France 24)

2026–27 European windstorm season Portugal closes approximately 8,000 schools nationwide and suspends non-essential public services as Storm Charles approaches. The second day of the Web Summit in Lisbon is also cancelled. (AP) (Deadline)

China–Germany relations The German defence ministry announces that the Bundeswehr will discontinue using Chinese-made drones for military training and exercises, replacing them with German or other European models to address security concerns. (AP) (Reuters)
Kenya–Sudan relations Kenyan president William Ruto signs a deal for Sudan to lift its 20-month ban on imports of tea from Kenya. (Business Daily Africa)
2026 European infrastructure disruption European bomb threat wave More than 6,000 schools across Italy are evacuated following bomb threats. (BBC News) (Reuters)

Former Red Brigades member Leonardo Bertulazzi escapes house arrest in Buenos Aires, Argentina, while awaiting extradition to Italy to serve a 27-year prison sentence for kidnapping and membership in an armed group. Argentine security forces search for him. (AFP via France 24)
Colombian conflict Two people are arrested in connection with an explosive attack on the headquarters of Colombian broadcaster RCN Televisión in Cali, Valle del Cauca. (AFP via Gulf News)

2026 Brazilian general election The Brazilian Superior Electoral Court fines Meta Platforms R$7.5 million (US$1.34 million) for failing to comply with judicial orders concerning the 2026 Brazilian Presidential election, while finding insufficient evidence of deliberate electoral interference. (AFP via Le Monde)

2026 United States elections 2026 United States Senate elections 2026 United States Senate election in Mississippi After a week of counting affidavit ballots, CNN projects the election to the U.S. Senate in Mississippi for Democratic candidate Scott Colom, defeating the incumbent Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith and becoming the first black senator from the state since Blanche Bruce in the 1874–75 United States Senate elections. (CNN)
Independence March (Poland) Polish president Karol Nawrocki and at least 500,000 people participate in the annual patriotic march celebrating the National Independence Day in Warsaw, Poland. (Zero)
Russian ambassador to the United States Alexander Darchiev dies of a chronic illness. His death is announced by the Russian foreign ministry. (Reuters)
Pope Leo XIV leaves Argentina and arrives in Peru. Peru unveils a 14-meter (45-foot tall) statue of the Pope, described as the world's tallest of the pontiff. (IJR)

Cybersecurity firm CloudSek reports that the Kazakhstan-linked hacker group Silent Lynx used an autonomous agent to breach Tajikistan's government database and steal more than 2,000 national security-related documents. (Reuters) (The Record)
2026 FIFA U-17 World Cup The United States men's national under-17 soccer team withdraws from the upcoming FIFA U-17 World Cup in Qatar, citing safety concerns. (ESPN)
